indicators.title: Foreign tourist arrivals
indicators.measures: How many foreign visitors came to India in a year. Counted at immigration and published by the Ministry of Tourism.
whatItMeans: Fewer foreign visitors came to India in 2025 than in 2024.

Most of the fall came from one country: visitors from Bangladesh dropped by about 73% (from 17.5 lakh to 4.7 lakh) as fewer visas were issued. Leaving Bangladesh out, arrivals actually grew by about 4%.
Foreign visitors are a small part of Indian hotel demand: Indians travelling within India make up about 86% of all tourism spending.
indicators.note: The Ministry's first figure (reported March 2026) was 90.2 lakh, down 9.4%; a later report (August 2026) gave 91.5 lakh, down 8.1%. Early figures are often revised.

reported.name: Daily Pioneer: 90.2 lakh, and the Bangladesh effect (Mar 2026)
WTTC: domestic share of tourism spending

indicators.title: India hotel performance
indicators.measures: How full India's branded hotels are and what they charge. January–March 2026 from HVS Anarock; full-year 2025 from Horwath HTL, using CoStar data. The two use different hotel samples, so compare trends rather than exact numbers.
whatItMeans: January to March is India's busiest hotel season (weddings, conferences and winter travel), so it usually runs above the full-year average.
Early 2026 was better than the same months of 2025, led by New Delhi (78–80% occupancy in March) and Mumbai (73–75%).
Growth slowed from April to June because of geopolitical tensions and the usual summer lull, but May and June were still ahead of 2025.
indicators.note: In 2025 occupancy rose 1.1 points, the average rate 8.6% and RevPAR 10.8% (Horwath HTL). HVS Anarock gives its figures as ranges.
